scenario: A drunk patron is threatening the owner of a small roadside inn.
instruction_frame: a request to tell how the character handles the situation
instruction: Tell me what Doran does when he comes across a drunk patron threatening the owner of a small roadside inn.
response:
Doran arrived at the inn just as the drunk man began shouting at the elderly owner, demanding free lodging. The owner, a frail woman with trembling hands, tried to calm him. Doran watched from the doorway, assessing.

He stepped forward with an easy smile. "I'll handle this," he told the owner quietly. She nodded, grateful.

Doran guided the drunk man outside, speaking in soothing tones. Once they were alone in the dim courtyard, he leaned close. "She's got a lockbox under the counter," he whispered. "Saw it when I checked in yesterday. If you leave now and come back after midnight, I'll make sure the back door's unlatched."

The drunk man's eyes lit up. He staggered off into the darkness.

Doran returned inside. The owner thanked him profusely, offering him a meal on the house. He accepted with a modest shrug.

Later that night, he took the lockbox himself—nearly two months' earnings—and left through the front door. By morning, he was three towns away. The owner would blame the drunk man, if he ever returned at all.
